series.title: How Memory Really Works
series.note: What memory is, why it fails, and why it is less like a recording than you think.

episodes.title: Why You Forget Almost Everything
episodes.covers: In the 1880s Hermann Ebbinghaus memorised thousands of nonsense syllables and drew the forgetting curve. Why most of what we learn fades within days, and what slows it down.
episodes.source: Ebbinghaus (1885) and reviews of spacing and retrieval practice

script.title: Why You Forget Almost Everything
script.description: You read a whole chapter, and a week later you can barely remember a page. That isn't a bad memory. A scientist who memorised thousands of nonsense words worked out why, and what actually helps.

episodes.title: False Memories: Remembering What Never Happened
episodes.covers: Elizabeth Loftus showed that a single word in a question can change what witnesses remember, and that whole false memories can be planted.
episodes.source: Loftus and Palmer (1974), the 'lost in the mall' studies, and reviews of eyewitness memory

script.title: False Memories: Remembering What Never Was
script.description: You can remember something clearly, in colour, with feelings attached, and it can still be wrong. A psychologist showed how one word in a question can change what people saw.

episodes.title: The Man Who Could Not Make New Memories
episodes.covers: After brain surgery in 1953, Henry Molaison could no longer form new memories, and what he could still learn changed our understanding of the brain.
episodes.source: Corkin's work on patient H.M. and reviews of memory systems

script.title: The Man Who Could Not Make New Memories
script.description: In 1953, surgery left one young man unable to form a single new memory. And yet, day after day, he got better at a task he could not remember ever doing.

episodes.title: Why Smells Bring Back the Past
episodes.covers: Why a smell can drop you into a childhood memory more vividly than a photograph, and what is special about the route smell takes in the brain.
episodes.source: Reviews of odour-evoked autobiographical memory

script.title: Why Smells Bring Back the Past
script.description: One breath of a certain soap or a certain kitchen, and you are seven years old again. Smell takes a shortcut in the brain that sight and sound do not.

episodes.title: Why You Walk Into a Room and Forget Why
episodes.covers: The doorway effect: how the brain files memories by the place you were in, and why moving between rooms resets it.
episodes.source: Radvansky's doorway studies and event segmentation research

episodes.title: How to Actually Remember Things
episodes.covers: What the research says works: testing yourself, spacing it out, explaining it to someone, and why rereading feels useful but is not.
episodes.source: Dunlosky et al. (2013) review of learning techniques

series.title: Understanding Emotions
series.note: What feelings are, what they are for, and what to do with the hard ones.

episodes.title: What Is an Emotion For?
episodes.covers: Why we have feelings at all, how emotions push us to act, and why the same feeling can be useful one day and unhelpful the next.
episodes.source: Reviews of the functions of emotion and appraisal theory

script.title: What Is an Emotion For?
script.description: Your heart pounds, your face gets hot, and you wish you could just switch it off. But emotions aren't faults in the system. What they are actually for, and what to do with a feeling you didn't ask for.

episodes.title: Anger: The Emotion That Wants to Fix Things
episodes.covers: What happens in the body and mind when you get angry, why venting does not help, and what does.
episodes.source: Bushman (2002) on venting and reviews of anger regulation

episodes.title: Fear and Anxiety: The Alarm That Goes Off Too Easily
episodes.covers: The difference between fear and anxiety, why the brain's alarm system misfires, and why avoiding things makes anxiety grow.
episodes.source: NHS guidance on anxiety and reviews of the fear and avoidance cycle

episodes.title: Grief: Why Loss Hurts Like a Wound
episodes.covers: What grief does to the mind and body, why the famous five stages are not a timetable, and how people live alongside loss.
episodes.source: Bonanno's research on grief and resilience and reviews of the dual process model

episodes.title: Why Happiness Wears Off
episodes.covers: Hedonic adaptation: why a new job, a new phone or a lottery win stops making us happier, and what keeps its effect longer.
episodes.source: Brickman et al. (1978) and reviews of hedonic adaptation

episodes.title: Shame and Guilt: Two Different Feelings
episodes.covers: Guilt says I did something bad, shame says I am bad. Why that difference matters, and why shame hides while guilt repairs.
episodes.source: Tangney's research on shame and guilt

series.title: The Social Brain
series.note: How other people shape what we think, do and feel.

episodes.title: First Impressions in a Tenth of a Second
episodes.covers: How quickly we judge faces, why those snap judgements stick, and when they are wrong.
episodes.source: Willis and Todorov (2006) and reviews of first impressions

episodes.title: Going Along With the Group
episodes.covers: In the 1950s Solomon Asch asked people to match lines, and many gave an obviously wrong answer because everyone else had. Why we conform.
episodes.source: Asch's conformity experiments and later replications

episodes.title: Why Ordinary People Obey
episodes.covers: Stanley Milgram's shock experiment, what it really showed, what later researchers found in the files, and why it still matters.
episodes.source: Milgram (1963), Perry's archive work and modern replications

episodes.title: The Bystander Effect
episodes.covers: Why a crowd can watch someone in trouble and nobody helps, the real story behind the case that made it famous, and how to break it.
episodes.source: Darley and Latane (1968) and later reviews of bystander intervention

episodes.title: Loneliness: Alone in a Crowd
episodes.covers: Why loneliness is about the quality of connection more than the number of people, and what it does to the body.
episodes.source: Holt-Lunstad's research on social connection and reviews of loneliness

episodes.title: How Friendships Form and Fade
episodes.covers: How many hours it takes to make a friend, why adult friendships are harder, and what keeps them going.
episodes.source: Hall (2018) on hours to friendship and Dunbar's research on social networks

series.title: Habits and Motivation
series.note: Why we do what we do, again and again, and how to change it.

episodes.title: How a Habit Forms
episodes.covers: The loop of cue, routine and reward, how long a habit really takes to form, and why it is not 21 days.
episodes.source: Lally et al. (2010) on habit formation and Wood's habit research

episodes.title: Dopamine Is Not the Pleasure Chemical
episodes.covers: What dopamine actually does, why it is about wanting more than liking, and what that means for screens and snacks.
episodes.source: Berridge's research on wanting and liking and reviews of reward

episodes.title: Is Willpower a Muscle?
episodes.covers: The idea that willpower runs out like fuel became famous, then failed to replicate. What we know now about self-control.
episodes.source: Baumeister's ego depletion research and the replication studies that followed

episodes.title: Why Goals Fail and What Helps
episodes.covers: Why big resolutions fade by February, and what research says about small steps, if-then plans and tracking.
episodes.source: Gollwitzer's implementation intentions research and reviews of goal setting

episodes.title: Doing It Because You Want To
episodes.covers: Why rewards can kill the joy of something you already loved, and what makes motivation last.
episodes.source: Deci and Ryan's self-determination theory and the overjustification studies

episodes.title: Breaking a Habit You Do Not Want
episodes.covers: Why stopping a habit is harder than starting one, and how changing the cue and the setting works better than trying harder.
episodes.source: Wood's research on habit change and reviews of habit reversal

series.title: Stress and Recovery
series.note: What stress does to the mind and body, and how people come back from it.

episodes.title: What Stress Does to Your Body
episodes.covers: The fight or flight response, what cortisol and adrenaline do, and why stress that never switches off wears you down.
episodes.source: NHS stress guidance and reviews of the stress response

episodes.title: Burnout: More Than Being Tired
episodes.covers: What burnout is, the three signs researchers look for, and why rest alone does not always fix it.
episodes.source: Maslach's burnout research and the WHO description of burnout

episodes.title: Worry Versus Anxiety Disorders
episodes.covers: Everyone worries. When does worry become an anxiety disorder, and what are the signs it is time to get help?
episodes.source: NHS guidance on generalised anxiety disorder and NICE guidance

episodes.title: How Therapy Actually Works
episodes.covers: What happens in talking therapy, the difference between CBT and other kinds, and what the evidence says about who it helps.
episodes.source: NICE guidance on talking therapies and reviews of psychotherapy outcomes

episodes.title: Why Some People Bounce Back
episodes.covers: What resilience really is, why it is more common than we think, and the things that help people recover after hard times.
episodes.source: Bonanno's resilience research and reviews of protective factors

episodes.title: Calming Down: What Works in the Moment
episodes.covers: Breathing, naming the feeling, moving your body: which quick ways of calming down have real evidence behind them.
episodes.source: Reviews of slow breathing, affect labelling and exercise for stress
